Starting from any vertex, it must have at least 4 neighbors (distance 1). 
Each of these 4 neighbors must have at least 3 additional neighbors to maintain a minimum degree of 4. Since the girth is at least 8, there can be no cycles of length 7 or less, meaning all these new neighbors must be distinct. This gives 4 * 3 = 12 vertices at distance 2.
Similarly, each of these 12 vertices must have at least 3 additional distinct neighbors, giving 12 * 3 = 36 vertices at distance 3.
Summing these up, a graph with minimum degree 4 and girth 8 requires at least 1 (root) + 4 (dist 1) + 12 (dist 2) + 36 (dist 3) = 53 vertices. 
Since the problem asks for a graph with only 18 vertices, it is mathematically impossible.
